findings.reason: The wrapper invokes f only once, saves the recovered panic value in d.p, and uses that value for subsequent panics.
The wrapper stores f's result once and returns it directly. A stored pointer still points to the same object, so later mutations are visible through it.
OnceFunc stores the function value supplied at construction and invokes that stored value. Reassigning the caller's variable does not change the stored value.

cases.claim: Copying the function returned by OnceFunc shares its once state; calling both function values invokes the original function once.
Two separate OnceFunc calls wrapping the same function share one once state.
If the original function panics, repeated calls re-panic with the same value without executing the original function again.
If OnceValue returns a pointer, later mutation of the pointed-to object is visible through subsequent returns of that same pointer.
Reassigning only the caller function variable after constructing OnceFunc changes which function the wrapper invokes.
After recovering the first OnceFunc panic, calling the wrapper again returns normally.
The application must retry an initialization function after every panic.
